heroSummary: The Bambu Lab X1C handles Polymaker PolyLite PETG exceptionally well out of the box with its direct-drive extruder and hardened steel nozzle. By capping the maximum volumetric speed at 14 mm³/s, the printer reliably prints at speeds up to 167 mm/s without experiencing under-extrusion or loss of layer adhesion.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate (or Smooth PEI with Glue Stick as a release agent to prevent tearing)
slicerTweaks: Set Maximum Volumetric Speed to 14 mm³/s in the filament settings to automatically limit line speeds to 167 mm/s.
Adjust Nozzle Temperature to 240°C and Bed Temperature to 75°C across all layers for balanced flow and adhesion.
Enable 'Wipe while retracting' with a distance of 2.0 mm to mitigate fine PETG surface stringing and nozzle buildup.
Keep the top glass lid propped or the front door unlatched if the enclosure chamber exceeds 40°C to eliminate heat creep risks.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Severe stringing and fine hair buildup
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PETG is hygroscopic and oozes significantly when moisture expands in the melt zone, exacerbated by excessive nozzle temperature.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the filament spool in a blast dryer at 65°C for 6 to 8 hours and ensure retraction is set to 0.8 mm at 35 mm/s with Z-hop set to 'Normal Auto'.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Build plate surface damage / tearing on part removal
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PETG bonds aggressively to bare smooth PEI surfaces, creating a bond stronger than the PEI coating itself.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Switch to a Bambu Textured PEI plate or apply a thin, uniform layer of PVP glue stick/liquid glue as a sacrificial release agent on smooth plates.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Layer delamination or brittle structural parts
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Excessive auxiliary cooling or high part cooling fan speeds exceeding 60% cooling the molten bead too rapidly.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Disable the auxiliary chamber fan completely and clamp maximum part cooling fan speed to 60% with a minimum threshold of 20%.

faq.question: Can I print Polymaker PolyLite PETG at the Bambu X1C default 250-300 mm/s profile speeds?
faq.answer: No, standard PolyLite PETG has a melt flow rate limited to roughly 14 mm³/s, meaning attempts to print above 167 mm/s at 0.2mm layer height will cause severe under-extrusion and matte, weak layers.

faq.question: Should I print PETG with the X1C door closed or open?
faq.answer: Keep the top glass vented or the door cracked open during long prints to prevent chamber temperatures exceeding 40°C, which can cause direct-drive heat creep.

faq.question: Does PolyLite PETG require nozzle hardening on the X1C?
faq.answer: No, PolyLite PETG is non-abrasive, though the X1C's stock hardened steel nozzle works perfectly without requiring any hardware changes.

faq.question: What Pressure Advance (PA) value should I calibrate for PolyLite PETG on the X1C?
faq.answer: PolyLite PETG typically calibrates to a PA value between 0.032 and 0.042 s on the Bambu direct drive extruder, which eliminates bulging corners.
